title: Agentic AI: Three Operator Cases
points: Voltage support, service restoration and cyber response
120 minutes with three short group exercises
IEEE ComSoc theme / Recorded research examples and operator review
note: This is the follow-on to the agentic-AI foundations tutorial. We apply the ideas to three engineering decisions, rather than repeating the literature survey. The numerical examples come from the existing GridGuard teaching studies. Their models and assumptions differ: a synthetic distribution feeder, a six-node restoration transport graph, and a four-bus DC estimation fixture. None is a live utility deployment or a permission to operate equipment. All slides belong to the session. The three exercises require discussion and a decision, not software installation.

title: Three cases test three different kinds of evidence
caption: The same advisory process must answer a different engineering question in each case.
points: Voltage: does the proposed control pass the required model scope?
Restoration: who receives service? Cyber: which information can support a decision?
note: Ask participants to predict which evidence can fail in each case. Voltage has a model-coverage problem: a candidate can pass a reduced model and fail a broader AC audit. Restoration has an explicit objective and topology problem: maximum total load and priority service can legitimately produce different plans. Cyber has an information-trust problem: a small residual can coexist with a wrong estimated state. These are not interchangeable failure modes, so one universal success percentage is inappropriate. Keep the cases separate while reusing the habit of specifying inputs, tools, tests and the human decision.

title: An operator request becomes a checked study
caption: Proposed advisory workflow. Numerical checks control whether a candidate reaches human review.
points: The agent interprets the request and chooses allowed tools. Solvers calculate the consequences.
Failed or outdated evidence returns to a bounded repair step, or the study stops.
note: Read the workflow as responsibilities, not a claim that each box is a separate LLM. Awareness fixes the study state. Planning proposes an allowed action. Simulation produces numerical evidence. Verification tests the request, limits and evidence identity. The optimizer or repair step may suggest a new candidate within a fixed budget. A person receives the resulting advisory packet. This structure is a teaching synthesis informed by the existing classroom implementation. The engineering notebooks use a custom Python supervisor. Their shared responsibilities do not establish that they execute in LangGraph; the separate graph lab demonstrates that runtime independently. A numerical solver or fixed script may perform most of the work. The added walkthroughs expose the actual recorded choices, code calls, output values and pending human decisions. The voltage P3 workflow and the standard restoration/cyber workflow are separate dated studies. Each uses its original custom Python supervisor. The present GridGuard app has a separate LangGraph implementation; these archived records do not test that newer runtime.

title: Every result must stay attached to its inputs
caption: Illustrative evidence identity. These version labels are teaching examples, not an operational record.
points: Keep the case, model scope, data revision, candidate and limits together.
A matching hash detects a changed packet. It does not prove that a sensor or a model is correct.
note: Use a concrete example: a voltage result at load multiplier 1.00 cannot support a changed request at 1.10 without checking applicability. Likewise, a restoration capacity change or a different measurement-trust set changes the evidence context. The classroom binding routine hashes canonicalized request, candidate and result contents. That establishes local content consistency only. It is not a digital signature, sensor authentication, or a proof of physical feasibility. The operator should be able to see the relevant identity and limits directly in the report. Do not transfer all details into a cryptographic-looking identifier that nobody can inspect.

title: The three exercises end with a specific next step
points: Work in pairs: one person proposes the next step, the other checks the evidence.
For each case, choose: continue the study, hold the recommendation, or request missing evidence.
Use one number or one failed check to explain the decision. Each discussion lasts four minutes.
note: Explain the active-learning format before the first case. Give pairs one minute to read, two minutes to decide and one minute to prepare a short justification. The debrief follows as a separate slide, so the answer is not hidden behind a click or given away on the exercise slide. The choices concern progression through an advisory study, not field dispatch. Encourage participants to name the next responsible tool or human role. A valid hold decision should specify what evidence would allow progress.

title: Numerical tools propose; the language model selects a trial
points: MPC solves three forecast snapshots and proposes its first move.
SAC proposes from saved trained weights. An LLM selects a permitted trial after numerical checks.
caption: Native workflow for the existing implementation; changed commands return to the solver.
note: MPC means model predictive control. Here it is a local sensitivity optimizer over H=3 quasi-static power-flow snapshots, linked by a command-movement penalty and discount 0.98. Only its first action enters the response-selection experiment. This is not a certified global optimum, dynamic stability study or robust recursive-feasibility proof. SAC means soft actor-critic: a model-free RL method. The supplied actor was trained previously using rewards from a declared OpenDSS response-surface approximation at nominal current allowance. Classroom inference uses saved weights without retraining; current derating is a transfer condition. Both tools produce candidate numerical commands. A fresh simulation and fail-closed checks decide whether a candidate can become the incumbent. Only then do actual local language models request a bounded refinement from the allowed menu. They do not solve the power flow, relax limits or grant approval. Cite the local implementation for every measured result; the MPC book and SAC paper explain the algorithm families, not performance of this feeder. title: WLS finds the best common explanation
diagram_spec: An equal-precision scalar illustration: two readings 9 and 11 fit a common estimate 10, leaving residuals -1 and +1. Connect the number-line example to the weighted least-squares objective sum of squared residuals divided by sigma squared. Label the scalar illustration separately from the four-bus run.
points: A residual is a reading minus the value predicted by the estimated state.
WLS gives more weight to a reading with a smaller stated noise scale.
caption: The 9–11 example explains fitting; the network calculation estimates three angles from eight readings.
note: Start with the scalar picture. Two equally precise readings of one quantity are 9 and 11. Choosing 10 leaves residuals -1 and +1; moving the estimate toward either reading increases the total squared mismatch. WLS extends this idea to the network predictions Hx. It minimizes the sum over readings of ((z_j-(Hx)_j)/sigma_j)^2. Here z is the reading vector, H maps angles to expected readings, and sigma_j is the assumed standard deviation of the reading noise. A smaller sigma creates a larger penalty for the same raw mismatch. It expresses the estimator's stated precision model, not a cybersecurity trust judgment. The supplied code solves the full-rank weighted problem numerically using least squares. Flow noise scales are 0.004 p.u., injection noise scales 0.006 p.u., and the angle-1 noise scale is 0.0005 rad. Do not interpret unequal weights as proof that a channel is authentic.

title: A residual alarm checks consistency
diagram_spec: A horizontal J axis places the actual nominal statistic 3.92022 below a red threshold 15.0863. Shade only the upper-tail alarm region. Show eight readings minus rank three gives five degrees of freedom and alpha=1%. Clearly separate a consistency test from sensor authenticity.

The 1% calibration assumes the correct linear model and the stated independent Gaussian noise.

note: The statistic is J=r^T R^-1 r, where r=z-Hxhat and R is the diagonal matrix of the assumed noise variances. Under the stated linear Gaussian model, correct H and covariance, and full column rank, the minimized statistic has m-rank(H)=5 degrees of freedom. The 99th percentile is 15.0862724694; use 15.0863 on the slide. Nominal J is 3.9202216910. Alpha=0.01 is a nominal upper-tail false-alarm probability under those assumptions. It is not a 99% chance that the data are safe, nor the probability that an attacker is present. An isolated +0.08 p.u. change on flow12 produces J=277.4974469045 and an alarm in this seeded run. That is evidence of inconsistency, not an identification of the cause or a guarantee that all coordinated errors will be detected.

title: Coordinated changes can leave the residual unchanged

note: Return to the scalar illustration: shifting both readings by three moves their best common estimate by three, while the two residuals remain -1 and +1. The linear network identity is z'=z+Hc, xhat'=xhat+c and r'=r when the same full-rank H and weights are used. Here c is a shift in the inferred angle state; Hc is the corresponding change in model predictions. Liu, Ning and Reiter establish this limitation of residual-based bad-data detection. Their result has specific access and model assumptions; it is not a claim that any attacker can alter every utility state estimate. Protected measurements restrict which changes are possible. The synthetic workshop deliberately supplies a matching coordinated perturbation as a negative control, so it can test whether a residual-only workflow mistakes consistency for trust. We do not discuss targeting real measurement channels. The operator lesson is to seek independent evidence when the trust premise is unresolved, even if the residual test is quiet.

The left panel's symmetric-log scale accommodates small and large statistics. The right panel compares the estimate with the known state supplied by the synthetic experiment.
